title: Grain Accounting Manual: The Life of a Contract Under Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
A contract under Grain Marketing Contracts moves through its life on recorded facts rather than on anybody's say-so.

**Binding.** The grain desk countersigns an application once the programme's paperwork is on file, and only then does the contract bind either side.

**Delivering, and fully delivered.** The first load applied moves it into delivering, and the load that takes the bushels still owed to zero moves it to fully delivered; both of those follow from the ledger and neither is set by hand.

**Settled.** A fully delivered contract is closed out to settled once every delivered bushel has been priced and every statement drawn on it has been paid, so a contract carrying an unpriced parcel or an unpaid statement stays open however complete the deliveries look. Both conditions are required together: every parcel priced, and every statement paid.

**Default.** Where the last day of the delivery window passes with bushels still owed and neither a roll nor a buyout was arranged, the contract goes to default, the undelivered bushels carry the programme's default penalty per bushel in addition to the market loss, and the matter leaves the desk for the credit department.

**Terminal standings.** Cancellation and default are both terminal: a cancelled or defaulted contract is never reopened, and a member who wants the bushels back must be written a new contract at the day's terms.

## The two conditions on settled, in combination

| Every delivered bushel priced | Every statement drawn on the contract paid | Standing reached |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | settled |
| Yes | No | stays fully delivered |
| No | Yes | stays fully delivered |
| No | No | stays fully delivered |
